consensus_summary: Across the blind responses, anointing primarily symbolizes consecration—setting a person apart for sacred office or mission—joined to empowerment by the Holy Spirit, with oil commonly read as a type of the Spirit; this culminates in Christ as the Anointed One and extends to believers. Healing, joy/hospitality, and burial uses are secondary, context-dependent senses.
book_summary: Anointing means marking a person or thing as God’s own and appointing it to a stated office or work; oil may supply the visible mark, the Spirit may supply the power, and the work shows what the appointment is for. The common view is faulted for equating anointing with the Spirit’s empowering presence without distinguishing appointment, sign, power, and office.
consensus_core_identification: Consecration/setting apart for holy office plus Holy Spirit empowerment (oil as Spirit-symbol), centered on Messiah and sacred offices.
book_core_identification: Marking as God’s own and appointing to a stated office or work, with oil, Spirit, and work distinguished as mark, power, and purpose.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus treats Spirit-empowerment (and oil-as-Spirit) as intrinsic to the primary meaning; the book keeps appointment/marking as the core and reclassifies Spirit power and oil as optional accompanying roles, also explicitly covering things (e.g. tabernacle) and non-Yahwist appointees (e.g. Cyrus) without fusing them to charismatic Spirit endowment.
material_contradiction: None on the shared referent of divine appointment/consecration; the disagreement is over whether Spirit empowerment is definitional of anointing or only a possible concurrent factor.
rationale: Both cores name divine setting-apart for office or work, so the central referent is not replaced. The book materially tightens the definition by separating mark, power, and office and by correcting the common collapse into ‘the Spirit’s empowering presence,’ which narrows and re-boundaries cases the consensus bundles together—hence REFINED with BOOK_NARROWS and PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION, not MATCH or DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: Acts 10:38 and 1 Sam 16:13 tightly join anointing with the Spirit and power, so the consensus may argue Spirit empowerment is not merely optional accompaniment but part of what biblical anointing essentially signifies.
